$comment: The wizard corpus, and an honest account of what it is not.
StarCraft II ships the format specification and zero wizard files: a scan of the installed
game found 666,588 CASC paths across 70 extensions and no .BlizWiz among them. Wizards are
written by map and mod authors, so there is no vendor corpus to check a parser against.
Author-written wizards do exist locally; they are listed in corpus.json and read in place by
wizard-corpus.test.ts rather than copied here, because their licence is not established.
Everything listed below is spec-derived: assembled by hand from the examples in
authoritative about the format, so these files exercise the real grammar — but they were
written by the same reasoning that wrote the parser, and a parser checked only against its
author's idea of the format is exactly how MK2 ended up with a parser for four elements that
editorSaved is therefore empty and is the open item. Filling it means opening the SC2 Editor,
building wizards that cover the specification, and using Manage Wizards > Export: files saved
by the program itself are an oracle that comes from Blizzard rather than from us. Until then
the round-trip and coverage tests prove the model is complete against these files only.

editorSaved.source: SC2Editor 5.0.16 Manage Wizards > Export of every wizard in artifacts/editor-acceptance-2026-09-15/wizards (2026-09-15); byte-exact, marked -text in .gitattributes
editorSaved.observed: UTF-8 without BOM, lowercase encoding="utf-8", CRLF, 4-space indent, no final newline; comments dropped; T5a/T5b roots rewritten into one <wizardfile>; imported names get an " Import" suffix; children reordered (input: item, name, default, loadvalue, layout, reloadfrom, condition); an empty <layout/> always written and an empty <objecttypes/> when none is known; <count> inside <input>, value="" and <default value=""/> dropped; unknown object type Ability dropped (Abil kept); untyped validate, entry without type and id, and input="Sub;Flag" kept; text escapes > " '

specDerived.covers: the prototype wizard the specification's examples describe: inputs of every documented kind, named and inline conditions, all three validation types, the eight documented macros, and the WireframeVariations_Number entry example verbatim

the remainder of the specification: hidden wizards, an embedded wizard reached through type="Wizard:<id>" and the SubWizard:Input token spelling, every match and operator value, nested condition logic, layout minheight/minwidth, item count with ITEMINDEX, entry count with ENTRYINDEX, field count/index/cache/loadinput, useloaded and parentid, tokens, a literal ^^, and catalog references in both the value and the trailing-# count form
